title.en: The Web and HTTP: how many round trips a page takes
title.zh: 万维网与 HTTP：一个页面要多少个往返

description.en: Understand why a web page needs many requests, how many round trips each of HTTP's three connection styles costs, and how HTTP recognises you through cookies and saves repeated fetches through caching.
description.zh: 弄懂一个网页为什么要多次请求，HTTP 的三种连接方式各花几个往返，以及 HTTP 怎样靠 cookie 认出你、靠缓存省掉重复的取。

name.en: Web pages, objects, URLs and HTTP's request-response model
name.zh: 网页、对象、URL 与 HTTP 的请求—响应模型 (web objects, URL, HTTP client/server)
非持久 HTTP 与往返时间 (non-persistent HTTP, RTT)
持久 HTTP 与流水线 (persistent HTTP, pipelining)
HTTP 请求报文与方法 (request message, request methods)

name.en: HTTP response messages and status codes
name.zh: HTTP 响应报文与状态码 (response message, status codes)
Cookie 与无状态的 HTTP (cookies, stateless protocol)
网页缓存与代理服务器 (web caching, proxy server)

description.en: Thinks opening a web page means fetching one file with one request; in fact a page is made of many objects, and each object needs a request.
description.zh: 以为打开一个网页就是取一个文件、一次请求；其实一个页面由很多对象组成，每个对象都要请求。

description.en: Forgets that setting up the TCP connection itself takes 1 RTT; in non-persistent HTTP each object costs 2 RTTs, not 1.
description.zh: 忘了建立 TCP 连接本身也要 1 个 RTT；非持久 HTTP 的每个对象是 2 个 RTT，不是 1 个。

description.en: Thinks a persistent connection means the server remembers you; in fact it only reuses the same TCP connection, and HTTP is still stateless.
description.zh: 以为持久连接就是服务器记住了你；其实它只是复用同一条 TCP 连接，HTTP 仍然是无状态的。

description.en: Thinks non-persistent connections can also be pipelined; pipelining means sending requests back to back on the same persistent connection.
description.zh: 以为非持久连接也能流水线；流水线要在同一条持久连接上连续发请求。

description.en: Thinks POST data is encrypted; it is merely not put in the URL, and the entity body is still plain text.
description.zh: 以为 POST 的数据是加密的；它只是不放在网址里，实体体里仍然是明文。

description.en: Thinks the shopping cart is stored inside the cookie; in fact the cookie holds only a number, and the real state is in the server's database.
description.zh: 以为 cookie 里装着购物车；其实里面只有一个编号，真正的状态在服务器的数据库里。

description.en: Thinks what is in a cache is always the latest; in fact the object may already have changed on the origin server, and a conditional request is needed to check.
description.zh: 以为缓存里的永远是最新的；其实对象可能已经在源服务器上改了，要靠条件请求核对。

chapter.en: A page is not one file
chapter.zh: 一个页面不是一个文件

title.en: Take a guess first

prompt.en: A web page consists of 1 HTML file plus 10 images, 11 objects in all, all on the same server. Use the earliest style of HTTP: every object gets a new TCP connection, closed after the fetch, and the objects are fetched one after another. Round-trip time (RTT) is how long a small packet takes to go to the server and back. Ignoring file transfer time, how many RTTs do you wait to open the whole page?
prompt.zh: 一个网页由 1 个 HTML 文件加 10 张图片组成，一共 11 个对象，都在同一台服务器上。用最早的 HTTP 用法：每个对象都新建一条 TCP 连接，取完就关，一个接一个地取。往返时间 RTT 指一个小包到服务器再回来要多久。不计文件传输时间，打开整个页面要等几个 RTT？

label.en: 11 RTTs: one round trip per object
label.zh: 11 个 RTT：每个对象一个往返

feedback.en: Before sending the request for each object, a TCP connection must first be set up, and setting up the connection itself takes a round trip.
feedback.zh: 每个对象在发请求之前，还要先建一条 TCP 连接，建连接本身也要一个往返。

feedback.en: That looks like setting up the connection once and then adding 11 requests. But in the earliest style every object needs a new connection.
feedback.zh: 这像是只建了一次连接，再加 11 次请求。但最早的用法每个对象都要新建连接。

feedback.en: Right. Each object takes 2 RTTs: 1 to set up the connection, 1 for the request and response.
feedback.zh: 对。每个对象 2 个 RTT：1 个建连接，1 个请求和响应。

feedback.en: Each object needs only 2 RTTs (1 for the connection, 1 for the request and response), not 3.
feedback.zh: 每个对象只需要 2 个 RTT（建连接 1 个，请求响应 1 个），不是 3 个。

explain.en: Per object: 1 RTT to set up the connection, 1 RTT to send the request and receive the start of the response, 2 RTTs in all. With 11 objects, 11 × 2 = 22 RTTs. If the RTT is 50 ms, just waiting for round trips takes over 1 second. This lesson is about how to bring that down.
explain.zh: 每个对象：1 个 RTT 建连接，1 个 RTT 发请求、收响应开头，共 2 个 RTT。11 个对象，11 × 2 = 22 个 RTT。如果 RTT 是 50 ms，光是等往返就超过 1 秒。这一课就是看怎样把它压下来。

title.en: One click is really many requests
title.zh: 一次点击，其实是很多次请求

text.en: You click open a web page in your dorm and think you fetched one file. You didn't.
text.zh: 你在宿舍点开一个网页，以为是取了一个文件。其实不是。

text.en: A web page is made of many objects. An object is just a file: an HTML file, a JPEG image, a video. Most web pages are a base HTML file plus several objects it refers to. The browser first fetches the HTML, reads it, finds it says “put pic1.jpg, pic2.jpg ... here”, and fetches them one by one. So “opening a page” is many requests, not one.
text.zh: 一个网页由很多对象 (object) 组成。对象就是一个文件：HTML 文件、JPEG 图片、视频，都是。大多数网页是一个基础 HTML 文件 (base HTML file)，加上它引用的若干对象。浏览器先取回 HTML，读它，发现里面写着「这里放 pic1.jpg、pic2.jpg ……」，再逐个去取。所以「打开一个页面」是很多次请求，不是一次。

text.en: Each object is located by a URL (uniform resource locator), shaped like http://host/path. For example http://www.someschool.edu/someDept/pic.gif:
text.zh: 每个对象用一个 URL (uniform resource locator) 定位，形如 http://host/path。比如 http://www.someschool.edu/someDept/pic.gif：

items.en: **Host name**: www.someschool.edu. It must first be handed to DNS to become an IP (last lesson).
items.zh: **主机名** (host name)：www.someschool.edu。要先交给 DNS 变成 IP（上一课）。

items.en: **Path name**: someDept/pic.gif. It tells the server which of its files you want.
items.zh: **路径** (path name)：someDept/pic.gif。告诉服务器要它的哪个文件。

text.en: The calculations below use the example from the slides: 1 base HTML plus 10 JPEGs, 11 objects in all, all on the same server, and the base file's address is www.someschool.edu/someDepartment/home.html.
text.zh: 后面的计算要用到课件里的例子：1 个基础 HTML 加 10 张 JPEG，共 11 个对象，都在同一台服务器上，基础文件的地址是 www.someschool.edu/someDepartment/home.html。

title.en: A typo

body.en: One page in the slides writes this file as home.index, which is a typesetting slip. This lesson writes home.html throughout.
body.zh: 课件里有一页把这个文件写成了 home.index，应是排版笔误。本课统一写 home.html。

title.en: What the Web is made of

text.en: The World Wide Web (WWW) is not one thing but four things working together:
text.zh: 万维网 (World Wide Web，WWW) 不是一个东西，是四样东西配合：

rows.en: One end sends requests, the other responds

rows.zh: 浏览器 Firefox；Web 服务器 Apache

rows.en: Describes the structure and format of a page
rows.zh: 描述页面的结构和格式

rows.en: Makes a page come alive, generated dynamically
rows.zh: 让页面动起来，动态生成

rows.en: Specifies how clients and servers exchange information
rows.zh: 规定客户端和服务器怎样交换信息

text.en: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is an application-layer protocol that works by request and response. The browser is the client: it sends HTTP requests and displays the objects it receives. The web server receives requests and sends objects back packed into HTTP responses. One server can serve many clients at once.
text.zh: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) 是一个应用层协议，用请求—响应的方式工作。浏览器是客户端：发出 HTTP 请求，收到对象后显示。Web 服务器：收到请求，把对象装进 HTTP 响应送回去。一台服务器可以同时服务很多客户端。

text.en: HTTP rides on TCP: the browser first sets up a TCP connection to the server's port 80, then sends requests and receives responses over that connection. This is the starting point of all the calculations below: setting up a connection takes time, and going back and forth takes time.
text.zh: HTTP 靠 TCP 传输：浏览器先和服务器的 80 端口建一条 TCP 连接，再在这条连接上发请求、收响应。这就是下面所有计算的起点：建连接要时间，来回要时间。

title.en: One object, why two round trips
title.zh: 一个对象，为什么是两个往返

text.en: First make “a round trip” clear. Round-trip time (RTT): how long a small packet takes to go from the client to the server and back to the client. Fetching one object takes two round trips.
text.zh: 先把「一个往返」说清楚。往返时间 RTT (round-trip time)：一个小包从客户端到服务器、再回到客户端要多久。取一个对象，要经过两个往返。

The total time equals 2 RTTs plus the file transfer time.
alt.zh: 客户端与服务器之间的时序图：客户端发 SYN，服务器回 SYN-ACK，经过 1 个 RTT 连接建立；客户端发 ACK 加 HTTP 请求，服务器回响应，头几个字节到达又用了 1 个 RTT；之后是整个文件传完的时间。总时间等于 2 个 RTT 加文件传输时间。

caption.en: The slanted lines show the time packets spend on the way.
caption.zh: 斜线表示包在路上花的时间。

items.en: **1st RTT: set up the TCP connection.** The client sends SYN and the server replies SYN-ACK (the handshake from the transport-layer lessons). The moment the client receives it, the connection is open and it can send the request, which can go out together with the last acknowledgement of the handshake.
items.zh: **第 1 个 RTT：建立 TCP 连接。** 客户端发 SYN，服务器回 SYN-ACK（传输层那几课的握手）。客户端收到的那一刻，连接就通了，可以发请求，请求可以和握手的最后一个确认一起发出去。

items.en: **2nd RTT: request and response.** The request reaches the server, the server starts replying, and the first few bytes of the response get back to the client.
items.zh: **第 2 个 RTT：请求和响应。** 请求到服务器，服务器开始回，响应的头几个字节回到客户端。

items.en: **Plus file transfer time**: until the whole file has arrived.
items.zh: **再加文件传输时间**：整个文件到齐。

text.en: Why does setting up a connection take 1 RTT? Because the handshake goes back and forth: the client asks “can we connect?”, the server answers “yes”, and only then does the client know the other side is there and can receive. One question and one answer make one round trip.
text.zh: 为什么建连接就要 1 个 RTT？因为握手要来回：客户端问「能连吗」，服务器答「能」，客户端才知道对面在、能收。一问一答就是一个往返。

text.en: How long an RTT is depends on how far the road is: within a city it may be only a few milliseconds, across an ocean it can reach over a hundred. The slides' calculation treats every round trip as equally long, and below we set RTT = 50 ms.
text.zh: RTT 有多长，看路有多远：同城可能只有几毫秒，跨洋能到一百多毫秒。课件的算法按「每个往返一样长」，下面设 RTT = 50 ms。

title.en: Non-persistent HTTP: how many RTTs for 11 objects
title.zh: 非持久 HTTP：11 个对象要几个 RTT

intro.en: Non-persistent HTTP: one TCP connection carries at most one object. Fetching an object goes: connect to the server's port 80, send a request message, receive a response message, close the connection. The browser fetches the HTML, reads the 10 referenced JPEGs, and then does these four steps once for each image. Set RTT = 50 ms and ignore file transfer time.
intro.zh: 非持久 HTTP (non-persistent HTTP)：一条 TCP 连接最多传一个对象。取一个对象的过程是：连服务器的 80 端口，发请求报文，收响应报文，关连接。浏览器取回 HTML，读到 10 个被引用的 JPEG，再把这四步对每张图各做一遍。设 RTT = 50 ms，不计文件传输时间。

why.en: Per object: 1 RTT to set up the connection, 1 RTT for the request plus the start of the response. File transfer time is counted separately.
why.zh: 每个对象：1 个 RTT 建连接，1 个 RTT 请求加响应开头。文件传输时间另计。
1 个基础 HTML，加 10 张 JPEG。

why.en: The objects are fetched one after another, so the times add up.
why.zh: 对象一个接一个地取，时间相加。

why.en: With RTT at 50 ms, just waiting for round trips takes 1.1 seconds.
why.zh: RTT 是 50 ms 时，光是等往返就要 1.1 秒。

outro.en: Before even counting transfer, the page already waits over a second. And each object needs a connection opened and closed, with the server allocating buffers and other resources for every connection, which is extra overhead per connection. The trouble is that every object shakes hands all over again.
outro.zh: 还没算传输，页面已经要等一秒多。而且每个对象都要新建、关闭一条连接，服务器要为每条连接分配缓冲区之类的资源，这是每条连接的额外开销。问题出在：每个对象都重新握一次手。

title.en: Shake hands once, then use this connection for everything
title.zh: 握一次手，后面都走这条连接

text.en: The most natural improvement: shake hands once, and have the later objects all use this connection. This is persistent HTTP: after sending a response, the server does not close the connection. Later HTTP messages between the same client and server are all sent over this still-open connection. After the connection has been idle for a while, the server closes it.
text.zh: 最自然的改进：握一次手，后面的对象都走这条连接。这就是持久 HTTP (persistent HTTP)：服务器发完响应后，不关连接。同一对客户端和服务器之间后续的 HTTP 报文，都在这条还开着的连接上发。连接闲置一段时间之后，由服务器关闭。

text.en: The benefits:
text.zh: 好处：

items.en: **No repeated handshakes**: the handshake is done only once, and every later object saves 1 RTT.
items.zh: **省掉重复的握手**：握手只做一次，后面每个对象少 1 个 RTT。

items.en: **No per-connection overhead**: the server doesn't have to keep setting up and tearing down connections, uses fewer resources, and has higher request throughput.
items.zh: **省掉每条连接的额外开销**：服务器不用不停地建立、拆除连接，占的资源少，请求的吞吐量更高。

title.en: Beyond the slides: connecting to the last lesson
title.zh: 超出课件：和上一课连起来

body.en: The last lesson explained that a new TCP connection starts with cwnd at 1 and slow start. Non-persistent HTTP uses a new connection for every object, climbing from scratch each time; on a persistent connection the window has already grown, and later objects can carry on using it.
body.zh: 上一课讲过，新的 TCP 连接，cwnd 从 1 开始慢启动。非持久 HTTP 每取一个对象都是一条新连接，每次都从头爬；持久连接上的窗口已经涨起来了，后面的对象可以接着用。

text.en: The price is a hard question: when to close? An open connection isn't free; the server keeps memory for every open connection. A popular website has tens of thousands of visitors at once, each holding a persistent connection, and resources quickly run short. But if it closes too early, a request arrives just after closing, the benefit is lost, and another handshake is needed.
text.zh: 代价是一个难题：什么时候关？连接开着不是免费的，服务器要为每条开着的连接留内存。一个热门网站同时有几万个访客，每人占一条持久连接，资源很快就紧张。可如果关得太早，刚关就又有请求来，好处就没了，还要重新握手。

text.en: The server states its plan in the response headers, for example Keep-Alive: timeout=10, max=100, meaning: close this connection after 10 seconds idle, or after handling 100 more requests.
text.zh: 服务器会在响应首部里说出它的打算，比如 Keep-Alive: timeout=10, max=100，意思是：这条连接空闲 10 秒就关，最多再处理 100 个请求就关。

title.en: How many RTTs on a persistent connection

intro.en: The same page: 1 HTML plus 10 JPEGs. First, persistent but without pipelining: the client sends a request, waits for the response, and then sends the next. Set RTT = 50 ms and ignore transfer time.
intro.zh: 同一个页面：1 个 HTML 加 10 张 JPEG。先看持久连接但不流水线：客户端发一个请求，等响应回来，再发下一个。设 RTT = 50 ms，不计传输时间。

why.en: 1 RTT to set up the connection, only once; 1 RTT to fetch the HTML; then 10 images, 1 RTT each (request plus response).
why.zh: 1 个 RTT 建连接，只此一次；1 个 RTT 取回 HTML；之后 10 张图，各 1 个 RTT（请求加响应）。

why.en: Compared with non-persistent's 1100 ms, nearly half is saved.
why.zh: 对比非持久的 1100 ms，几乎省了一半。

why.en: Now add pipelining: as soon as the client reads the 10 references in the HTML, it sends all 10 requests at once, without waiting for the previous response. 1 RTT to set up the connection, 1 RTT to fetch the HTML, and 1 more RTT for the responses to all 10 images to come back together.
why.zh: 再加流水线 (pipelining)：客户端一读到 HTML 里的 10 个引用，就把 10 个请求一口气发出去，不等前一个响应。1 个 RTT 建连接，1 个 RTT 取 HTML，再 1 个 RTT，10 张图的响应一起回来。

why.en: For the same page, from 1100 ms down to 150 ms.
why.zh: 同一个页面，从 1100 ms 降到 150 ms。

outro.en: Pipelining can do this only on the premise of a persistent connection: the requests must be sent back to back on the same connection. With non-persistent connections, each object has its own new connection, and pipelining is impossible.
outro.zh: 流水线能做到这一步，前提是持久连接：请求要连续发在同一条连接上。非持久连接，每个对象一条新连接，没法流水线。

text.en: Pipelining has its limits:
text.zh: 流水线有它的限制：

items.en: **The HTML must arrive first**, to know which objects there are. So the minimum is 3 RTTs, never fewer.
items.zh: **必须先拿到 HTML**，才知道有哪些对象。所以最少也要 3 个 RTT，不会更少。

items.en: **With dependencies there is no parallelism**: if an object's address can only be known after reading the previous object (for example a stylesheet refers to another image), it has to wait for the previous one to come back.
items.zh: **有依赖就并行不了**：如果一个对象的地址，要读了前一个对象才知道（比如样式表里再引用一张图），就得等前一个回来。

summary.zh: 超出课件：现实里的浏览器

text.en: Browsers in practice open several connections at once (to one server, about 6 at a time is common), each connection fetching a few objects, spreading the time out with parallelism. HTTP/1.1 pipelining is rarely enabled in practice: on one connection, responses must come back in the order of the requests, so if an earlier one is slow, all the later ones are blocked (head-of-line blocking). Only the later HTTP/2 runs several requests at once on one connection, and truly solves this. The exam follows the three styles in the slides.
text.zh: 浏览器实际上会同时开多条连接（对同一台服务器，常见同时开 6 条左右），每条连接各取几个对象，用并行把时间摊开。HTTP/1.1 的流水线在现实里很少被启用：同一条连接上，响应必须按请求的顺序回来，前面一个慢，后面的全被堵住（队头阻塞）。后来的 HTTP/2 才在一条连接上同时跑多个请求，真正解决了它。考试按课件里的三种方式。

title.en: Count the total RTTs

prompt.en: A page consists of 1 HTML and 6 images, all on the same server. Ignore file transfer time. Which set gives, in order, the total RTTs for the three styles “non-persistent, sequential”, “persistent, no pipelining” and “persistent with pipelining”?
prompt.zh: 一个页面由 1 个 HTML 和 6 张图片组成，都在同一台服务器上。不计文件传输时间。下面哪一组，依次是「非持久、顺序」「持久、不流水线」「持久加流水线」三种方式的总 RTT？

feedback.en: The non-persistent entry counted only 1 RTT for each of the 7 requests, missing that a connection must be set up again before every object. Each object is 2 RTTs, 7 × 2 = 14.
feedback.zh: 非持久那一项只算了 7 个请求各 1 个 RTT，漏掉了每个对象前面都要重新建连接。每个对象是 2 个 RTT，7 × 2 = 14。

feedback.en: A persistent connection also spends 1 RTT setting up that one connection: 1 + 1 + 6 = 8, not 7. Pipelining is 1 + 1 + 1 = 3: until the HTML comes back you don't know which images there are, so the requests can't be sent ahead of time.
feedback.zh: 持久连接也要先花 1 个 RTT 建那一条连接：1 + 1 + 6 = 8，不是 7。流水线是 1 + 1 + 1 = 3：HTML 没回来之前，不知道有哪些图，请求没法提前发出。

feedback.en: Pipelining isn't added for nothing: after reading the HTML, the 6 requests go out at once, and only 1 RTT is needed for all of them to come back, so it is 3, not 8.
feedback.zh: 流水线不是白加的：读到 HTML 之后，6 个请求一口气发出，只要 1 个 RTT 就都回来了，所以是 3，不是 8。

explain.en: Non-persistent: 7 objects × 2 = 14. Persistent, no pipelining: 1 (connection) + 1 (HTML) + 6 (1 each) = 8. Persistent with pipelining: 1 + 1 + 1 = 3.
explain.zh: 非持久：7 个对象 × 2 = 14。持久、不流水线：1（建连接）+ 1（HTML）+ 6（各 1 个）= 8。持久加流水线：1 + 1 + 1 = 3。

title.en: Rebut “persistent connections are useless”
title.zh: 反驳「持久连接没什么用」

prompt.en: A classmate says: “A persistent connection just keeps the connection open, doesn't it? It's not much use, and it wastes resources.” Rebut this, and be fair: explain what a persistent connection actually saves, and what difficulty it brings.
prompt.zh: 同学说：「持久连接不就是让连接一直开着吗？没什么用，还白占着资源。」请你来反驳，并且公平一点：说清持久连接到底省了什么，又带来什么难题。

key_points.en: Reuses the same TCP connection, saving the repeated connection-setup handshake for each object, 1 RTT less per object
key_points.zh: 复用同一条 TCP 连接，省掉每个对象重复的建连接握手，每个对象少 1 个 RTT

key_points.en: Reduces per-connection overhead, raises request throughput, and also makes pipelining possible
key_points.zh: 减少每条连接的额外开销，提高请求的吞吐量，也让流水线成为可能

key_points.en: The main difficulty is when to close the connection: open too long and it ties up server resources, closed too early and it loses the benefit of persistence
key_points.zh: 主要难题是什么时候关闭连接：开得太久占用服务器资源，关得太早又失去持久连接的好处

model_answer.en: A persistent connection isn't just left open for nothing: it lets later requests reuse the same TCP connection, so there's no new handshake for each object and every object saves 1 RTT; the server also avoids the cost of repeatedly setting up and tearing down connections, so request throughput is higher, and it works together with pipelining. Its main difficulty is when to close: if a connection stays open too long it ties up server memory and other resources, which gets tight with many visitors; if it closes too early, a request arrives right after, and the benefit of reuse is lost.
model_answer.zh: 持久连接不是空开着：它让后续的请求复用同一条 TCP 连接，所以不用为每个对象重新握手，每个对象少 1 个 RTT，服务器也少了反复建连接、拆连接的开销，请求的吞吐量更高，还能配合流水线。它的主要难题是什么时候关：连接开得太久，会占着服务器的内存等资源，访客一多就吃紧；关得太早，刚关就又来请求，复用的好处就没了。

explain.en: The classmate is half right: the connection really is kept open. But being open is exactly where the benefit comes from, saving each object's handshake and each connection's overhead. The difficulty is there too: being open costs resources, and closing early loses the benefit, so you must weigh up “when to close”.
explain.zh: 同学说对了一半：连接确实一直开着。但开着正是好处的来源，省下的是每个对象的握手和每条连接的开销。难题也在这里：开着要花资源，关早了好处消失，所以要权衡「什么时候关」。

title.en: The request message: four parts

text.en: An HTTP message is text a person can read directly. A request message has four parts in order:
text.zh: HTTP 报文是人能直接读的文字。一条请求报文依次是四部分：

items.en: **Request line**: method, URL, version.
items.zh: **请求行** (request line)：方法、URL、版本。

items.en: **Header lines**: each line is “name: value”.
items.zh: **首部行** (header lines)：每行是「名字: 值」。

items.en: **A blank line**: marks the end of the headers.
items.zh: **一个空行**：标志首部结束。

items.en: **Entity body**: optional, data to hand to the server.
items.zh: **实体体** (entity body)：可选，要交给服务器的数据。

blocks.code:
GET /index.html HTTP/1.1
Host: www.unimelb.edu.au
User-Agent: Firefox/3.6.10
Accept: text/html,application/xhtml+xml
Accept-Language: en-us,en;q=0.5
Accept-Encoding: gzip,deflate
Accept-Charset: ISO-8859-1,utf-8;q=0.7
Keep-Alive: 115
Connection: keep-alive

caption.en: The example from the slides, with the host name changed to unimelb. Each line ends with a carriage return plus line feed; the final blank line marks the end of the headers. This one is a GET, with no entity body.
caption.zh: 课件的例子，主机名换成了 unimelb。每行末尾是回车加换行；最后的空行标志首部结束。这条是 GET，没有实体体。

text.en: What each header is for:
text.zh: 几个首部各管什么：

items.en: **Host**: which website is wanted. One server (one IP) can host many websites, and this line tells them apart. DNS gave only the IP, and the path doesn't carry the site name, so it is needed.
items.zh: **Host**：要哪个网站。一台服务器（一个 IP）上可以放很多网站，靠这一行区分。DNS 只给了 IP，路径里又不带网站名，所以需要它。

items.en: **User-Agent**: which browser I am.
items.zh: **User-Agent**：我是什么浏览器。

items.en: **Accept**: what types of content I can accept.
items.zh: **Accept**：我能接受什么类型的内容。

items.en: **Accept-Language**: which language I want. q=0.5 is a preference weight, from 0 to 1, the bigger the more wanted; when omitted it is 1.
items.zh: **Accept-Language**：我想要什么语言。q=0.5 是偏好权重，0 到 1，越大越想要；没写就是 1。

items.en: **Accept-Encoding**: which compression formats I can unpack. The server can compress before sending, saving transfer.
items.zh: **Accept-Encoding**：我能解开什么压缩格式。服务器可以压缩后再发，省传输。

items.en: **Accept-Charset**: which character encodings I recognise.
items.zh: **Accept-Charset**：我认哪些字符编码。

items.en: **Keep-Alive** and **Connection: keep-alive**: I'd like a persistent connection.
items.zh: **Keep-Alive** 和 **Connection: keep-alive**：我想用持久连接。

title.en: Methods: how to choose between GET and POST
title.zh: 方法：GET 和 POST 怎么选

text.en: The first word in the request line is the method, which says what you want to do with this URL:
text.zh: 请求行里的第一个词是方法 (method)，说明想对这个 URL 做什么：

rows.en: Read only a page's headers, not the content
rows.zh: 只读网页的首部，不要内容

rows.en: Append data to a named resource (such as a page)
rows.zh: 往一个命名的资源（如网页）追加数据

rows.en: The slides say “reserved for future use”; in practice proxies use it to set up tunnels
rows.zh: 课件写「保留给以后用」；现实中代理用它建立隧道

text.en: The most used are GET and POST. The difference between them lies mainly in where the data goes:
text.zh: 最常用的是 GET 和 POST。它们的区别，主要在数据放在哪里：

rows.en: Asking the server for something, and should not change anything on the server
rows.zh: 向服务器要东西，不该改变服务器上的东西

rows.en: Handing something to the server, such as submitting a form or uploading
rows.zh: 向服务器交东西，如提交表单、上传

rows.en: Does it show up in the URL
Yes: visible in the address bar, history and server logs
rows.zh: 会：地址栏、历史记录、服务器日志里都看得见

rows.en: Can it be cached or bookmarked

title.en: POST does not mean encrypted

body.en: Putting data in the entity body only keeps it out of the URL. The content is still plain text on the way, and anyone who intercepts it can read it. For secrecy, rely on HTTPS (Lesson 19).
body.zh: 数据放在实体体里，只是不出现在网址里。内容在路上仍然是明文，谁截到都能读。要保密，靠 HTTPS（第 19 课）。

title.en: Which method to submit a login

prompt.en: You enter your username and password on the university's single sign-on page and press submit. Which approach is more suitable?
prompt.zh: 你在学校的统一登录页输入用户名和密码，按下提交。下面哪种做法更合适？

label.en: Use GET, putting the username and password in the URL
label.zh: 用 GET，把用户名和密码拼在 URL 里

feedback.en: A URL shows up in the address bar, the browser history and server logs, where anyone passing by can see it. Data to hand to the server belongs in the entity body.
feedback.zh: URL 会出现在地址栏、浏览器历史记录和服务器日志里，谁路过都能看见。要交给服务器的数据，该放在实体体里。

label.en: Use POST, with the data in the entity body
label.zh: 用 POST，数据放在实体体里

label.en: Use POST, because the entity body is encrypted automatically
label.zh: 用 POST，因为实体体会自动加密

feedback.en: POST merely keeps the data out of the URL; the entity body is still plain text. Secrecy comes from HTTPS, not from the method.
feedback.zh: POST 只是不把数据放进网址，实体体里仍然是明文。保密要靠 HTTPS，不是靠方法。

label.en: Use HEAD, sending only the headers is enough
label.zh: 用 HEAD，只发首部就够了

feedback.en: HEAD fetches only the response headers, to inspect an object; it is not for submitting data.
feedback.zh: HEAD 只取响应的首部，用来检查对象，不是用来提交数据的。

explain.en: Use POST to submit data, with the data in the entity body, not in the URL. But that only removes one place for leaks; the transmission itself still needs HTTPS to be safe.
explain.zh: 提交数据用 POST，数据放在实体体里，不出现在网址里。但这只是少了一处泄露，传输本身还要靠 HTTPS 才安全。

title.en: The response message: how the server answers
title.zh: 响应报文：服务器怎样回话

text.en: The response message the server sends back is structured much like a request: status line, header lines, blank line, data.
text.zh: 服务器回的响应报文，结构和请求很像：状态行、首部行、空行、数据。

blocks.code:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Date: Sun, 26 Sep 2010 20:09:20 GMT
Server: Apache/2.0.52 (CentOS)
Last-Modified: Tue, 30 Oct 2007 17:00:02 GMT
Content-Length: 2652
Keep-Alive: timeout=10, max=100
Connection: Keep-Alive
Content-Type: text/html; charset=ISO-8859-1

data data data data data ...

caption.en: The response example from the slides.

items.en: **Status line**: protocol version, status code, description. 200 OK means success.
items.zh: **状态行** (status line)：协议版本、状态码、说明。200 OK 表示成功。

items.en: **Date**: when the response was generated. **Server**: the server software.
items.zh: **Date**：响应生成的时间。**Server**：服务器软件。

items.en: **Last-Modified**: when this object was last modified. Caches use it to judge whether something is out of date, as we will see later.
items.zh: **Last-Modified**：这个对象最后一次修改的时间。缓存靠它判断旧没旧，后面会用到。

items.en: **Content-Length**: how many bytes of data. On a persistent connection the connection is still open after the response ends, and the client relies on this to know where the object ends.
items.zh: **Content-Length**：数据有多少字节。持久连接上，响应结束后连接还开着，客户端要靠它知道这个对象到哪里结束。

items.en: **Keep-Alive: timeout=10, max=100** and **Connection: Keep-Alive**: this connection will be kept, closing after 10 seconds idle, and after at most 100 more requests.
items.zh: **Keep-Alive: timeout=10, max=100** 和 **Connection: Keep-Alive**：这条连接会保持，空闲 10 秒就关，最多再处理 100 个请求。

items.en: **Content-Type**: what type the data is and what encoding it uses.
items.zh: **Content-Type**：数据是什么类型、用什么编码。

items.en: After the blank line comes the data itself, such as the HTML file that was requested.
items.zh: 空行之后，是数据本身，比如请求的那个 HTML 文件。

title.en: Status codes: three digits, look at the first
title.zh: 状态码：三位数字，看第一位

text.en: A status code is three digits, divided into five classes by the first digit:
text.zh: 状态码是三位数字，按第一位分五类：

rows.en: 100: the server agrees to handle the request
200: request succeeded; 204: success, but no content
301: the page has moved; 304: the cached page is still valid
rows.zh: 301：页面搬家了；304：缓存的页面仍然有效

rows.en: 500: internal server error; 503: please try again later
rows.zh: 500：服务器内部错误；503：请稍后再试

text.en: Looking at just the first digit tells you “whose problem it is”: starting with 4, the request itself is at fault, blame the client; starting with 5, the server itself has gone wrong.
text.zh: 只看第一位，就能判断「谁的问题」：4 开头，是请求本身有问题，该怪客户端；5 开头，是服务器自己出了问题。

text.en: Put the status codes into a real exchange. A 301 goes like this:
text.zh: 把状态码放进真实的来回里。301 是这样的：

blocks.code:
请求：GET /old.html HTTP/1.1
响应：HTTP/1.1 301 Moved Permanently
      Location: http://www.someschool.edu/new.html
请求：GET /new.html HTTP/1.1
响应：HTTP/1.1 200 OK ...

caption.en: The Location header gives the new address; it doesn't appear in the slides, and is added here to make things clear.
caption.zh: Location 首部给出新地址，课件里没有出现，这里为了说清楚加上。

text.en: On seeing 301, the browser automatically goes to the new address and fetches again. To you it is just a page that moved house; to the network there is one more request, and so more round trips.
text.zh: 浏览器看到 301，就自动去新地址再取一次。对你来说，只是页面搬了家；对网络来说，多了一个请求，也就多了往返。

text.en: The story of 304 comes in the caching section: the server tells the cache “the copy you hold is still valid”, with no data in the response, saving a transfer.
text.zh: 304 的故事在缓存那一节：服务器告诉缓存「你手里那份还有效」，响应里不带数据，省下一次传输。

title.en: Which status code for which symptom

prompt.en: A classmate's website has three kinds of problems. (1) A letter was missing in the URL, and the file can't be found on the server. (2) A program on the server has a bug and crashed. (3) The administrator moved the page to a new address, and people still visit the old one. Which status code goes with each?
prompt.zh: 同学的网站出了三种问题。(1) 网址里少打了一个字母，服务器上找不到这个文件。(2) 服务器上的程序出了 bug，崩了。(3) 管理员把页面搬到了新地址，旧地址还有人访问。它们各对应哪个状态码？

feedback.en: Client error and server error are mixed up. A wrong URL is a problem with the request itself, starting with 4; a crashed program is the server's own problem, starting with 5.
feedback.zh: 把客户端错误和服务器错误弄反了。网址错是请求本身的问题，4 开头；程序崩了是服务器自己的问题，5 开头。

feedback.en: 301 is a redirect, saying the page has moved, and belongs with (3). A crashed program is a server error, starting with 5.
feedback.zh: 301 是重定向，说的是页面搬家了，应对应 (3)。程序崩了是服务器错误，5 开头。

feedback.en: 403 is access forbidden, not not-found; 304 means the cached page is still valid, not that the page has moved, which is 301.
feedback.zh: 403 是禁止访问，不是找不到；304 是缓存的页面仍有效，而不是页面搬家，搬家是 301。

explain.en: The first digit sets the class: starting with 4, blame the client (page not found is 404); starting with 5, blame the server (internal error is 500); starting with 3 is redirection (a move is 301, cache still valid is 304).
explain.zh: 第一位定类：4 开头怪客户端（找不到页面是 404），5 开头怪服务器（内部错误是 500），3 开头是重定向（搬家是 301，缓存仍有效是 304）。

title.en: Why the server can't recognise you
title.zh: 服务器为什么认不出你

text.en: HTTP is a stateless protocol: once the server has handled a request, it forgets it. When the next request comes, it treats it as a first meeting.
text.zh: HTTP 是无状态协议 (stateless protocol)：服务器处理完一个请求，就把它忘了。下一个请求来了，它只当是第一次见。

text.en: Why can't the server tell whether two requests come from the same person? Because a request has no “who I am” field. Can the IP address do it? No: many people in a dorm share one exit IP (NAT from Lesson 10), and even one person's IP changes.
text.zh: 为什么服务器分不清两次请求是不是同一个人？因为请求里没有「我是谁」这一栏。靠 IP 地址行不行？不行：宿舍里很多人共用一个出口 IP（第 10 课的 NAT），同一个人的 IP 也会变。

text.en: Being stateless has its good side: the server doesn't have to remember anything about each visitor, which is simple and easy to scale. But websites often need to recognise you:
text.zh: 无状态本身有好处：服务器不用为每个访客记任何东西，简单，容易扩展。可是网站常常需要认出你：

items.en: **Shopping cart**: you put an item in the cart, and when the next request opens the cart, the server has to know it is the same person.
items.zh: **购物车**：你把一件商品放进购物车，下一次请求再打开购物车，服务器得知道这是同一个人。

items.en: **Recommendations from your history**: the server has to match this request with your earlier activity.
items.zh: **按你的历史推荐**：服务器要把这次请求和你以前的活动对上。

title.en: A persistent connection is not remembering you
title.zh: 持久连接不等于记住你

body.en: A persistent connection only reuses the same TCP connection to save handshakes. The server still treats each request on the connection as an unrelated new request. HTTP is still stateless.
body.zh: 持久连接只是复用同一条 TCP 连接，省握手。连接上的每一个请求，服务器仍然当作互不相干的新请求。HTTP 依然是无状态的。

title.en: Cookies: let the browser remember a number for the server
title.zh: Cookie：让浏览器替服务器记一个号码

text.en: The way is to let the browser remember a number for the server, and send it with every request. This is the cookie. It is made of four parts working together:
text.zh: 办法是让浏览器替服务器记住一个编号，每次请求都带上。这就是 cookie。它由四部分配合：

items.en: The **Set-cookie** header in the response message.
items.zh: 响应报文里的 **Set-cookie** 首部。

items.en: The **Cookie** header in the request message.
items.zh: 请求报文里的 **Cookie** 首部。

items.en: The **cookie file** on the user's machine, managed by the browser.
items.zh: 用户机器上的 **cookie 文件**，由浏览器管理。

items.en: The **database** at the website's back end.
items.zh: 网站后台的**数据库**。

caption.en: Susan's first visit to amazon.com, and a week later.
caption.zh: Susan 第一次访问 amazon.com，以及一周之后。

text.en: Step by step:
text.zh: 一步一步：

items.en: Susan visits amazon.com for the first time. The request is ordinary, with no Cookie. The server generates a unique number 1678, creates a record indexed by 1678 in its back-end database, and adds a line `Set-cookie: 1678` to the response.
items.zh: Susan 第一次访问 amazon.com。请求是普通的，没有 Cookie。服务器生成一个唯一的编号 1678，在后台数据库里建一条以 1678 为索引的记录，并在响应里加一行 `Set-cookie: 1678`。

items.en: The browser receives it and adds a line to the cookie file it manages: www.amazon.com 1678. The file stores entries separately by website, so ebay's 8734 is in there too, unrelated.
items.zh: 浏览器收到，往它管理的 cookie 文件里添一行：www.amazon.com 1678。文件按网站分开存，所以 ebay 的 8734 也在里面，互不相干。

items.en: From then on, every request to amazon.com has the browser automatically add a line `Cookie: 1678`. The server looks up this number in the database and can track Susan's activity on this website.
items.zh: 以后每次向 amazon.com 请求，浏览器都自动加一行 `Cookie: 1678`。服务器按这个号码查数据库，就能追踪 Susan 在这个网站上的活动。

items.en: When she comes back a week later, the browser still carries 1678, and the server recognises her.
items.zh: 一周后她再来，浏览器仍然带着 1678，服务器认得她。

text.en: Be clear on one point: the cookie holds only a number. The real “state”, such as the cart and browsing history, is all in the server's database. The cookie is the key, not the safe.
text.zh: 要看清一点：cookie 里只有一个编号。购物车、浏览记录这些真正的「状态」，都在服务器的数据库里。cookie 是钥匙，不是保险箱。

title.en: Beyond the slides: privacy

body.en: The same number appears in every request you make to this website, so the website can string your behaviour together. The number itself doesn't contain your name, but in the database it can be matched with your account and behaviour. If many websites embed the same third party (such as an advertiser), that third party can also recognise you across different websites, which is why cookies cause privacy controversy.
body.zh: 同一个编号出现在你对这个网站的每一次请求里，网站就能把你的行为串起来。编号本身不含你的名字，但数据库里可以把它和你的账号、行为对上。如果很多网站都嵌入同一个第三方（比如广告），这个第三方还能在不同网站上认出你，这是 cookie 引起隐私争议的原因。

title.en: Where the shopping cart lives

prompt.en: On a shopping website you put 3 items in your cart, close the browser, and open it again the next day: the cart is still there. By the cookie model in the slides, where is the list of those 3 items most likely stored?
prompt.zh: 你在购物网站把 3 件商品放进购物车，关掉浏览器，第二天再打开，购物车还在。按课件里的 cookie 模型，这 3 件商品的清单最可能存在哪里？

label.en: In your cookie file, with the list sent to the server on every request
label.zh: 存在你的 cookie 文件里，每次请求都把清单带给服务器

feedback.en: A cookie stores just a number, not the cart's contents. If the list were kept in the cookie, it would have to be carried with every request, which is both clumsy and unreliable.
feedback.zh: cookie 里只存一个编号，不装购物车的内容。清单要是放在 cookie 里，每次请求都得带着，既笨重又不可靠。

label.en: In the website's back-end database, with the cookie holding only a number used to find it
label.zh: 存在网站后台的数据库里，cookie 里只有一个编号，用来找到它

label.en: In the HTTP protocol, with the server remembering the previous request itself
label.zh: 存在 HTTP 协议里，服务器自己记得上一次请求

feedback.en: HTTP is stateless, and the server forgets once it has handled a request. That is exactly why cookies are needed.
feedback.zh: HTTP 是无状态的，服务器处理完请求就忘了。正因为这样才需要 cookie。

label.zh: 存在你的 IP 地址里

feedback.en: An IP address is only an address and can't hold a list; besides, one person's IP changes, and many people share one IP.
feedback.zh: IP 地址只是一个编址，装不了清单；而且同一个人的 IP 会变，很多人还共用一个 IP。

explain.en: What the server gives you is a key: the number 1678. Each time the browser comes with it, the server uses it to dig your cart out of the database. Come back the next day, and as long as the cookie is still there, the server recognises you.
explain.zh: 服务器给你的是一把钥匙：编号 1678。浏览器每次带着它来，服务器就用它在数据库里翻出你的购物车。第二天再来，只要 cookie 还在，服务器就认得你。

title.en: Staying closer: proxies and caches
title.zh: 离得近一点：代理与缓存

text.en: Hundreds of people in the dorm open the same image on the same website. If each one makes a trip to a server at the far end of the world, isn't that wasteful?
text.zh: 宿舍里几百个人，打开同一个网站的同一张图。每个人都跑一趟远在天边的服务器，是不是太浪费？

text.en: The way: put a proxy server nearby, holding copies of objects fetched before, called a cache. A proxy is usually placed at an institution (university, company) or network provider. The browser is set up so that all HTTP requests go to the proxy first.
text.zh: 办法：在近处放一台代理服务器 (proxy server)，里面存着以前取过的对象的副本，叫缓存 (cache)。代理通常放在机构（学校、公司）或网络服务商那里。浏览器被设置成：所有 HTTP 请求先交给代理。

alt.en: Two clients send requests to the proxy server and receive responses along black arrows; the proxy server holds cached copies, and only on a miss does it ask the origin server for the object along orange arrows.
alt.zh: 两个客户端通过黑色箭头向代理服务器发请求并收响应；代理服务器内有缓存副本，只有未命中时才通过橙色箭头向源服务器要对象。

caption.en: The orange arrows are used only on a miss.
caption.zh: 橙色箭头只在未命中时才走。

items.en: **Hit**: the object is in the cache, and the proxy returns it directly.
items.zh: **命中** (hit)：对象在缓存里，代理直接返回。

items.en: **Miss**: the proxy asks the origin server for it on the client's behalf, keeps a copy, and passes it on to the client.
items.zh: **未命中** (miss)：代理替客户端向源服务器 (origin server) 要来，存一份，再转给客户端。

text.en: So a proxy is special: to the client it is a server; to the origin server it is a client.
text.zh: 所以代理很特别：对客户端，它是服务器；对源服务器，它是客户端。

text.en: There are three benefits: shorter response time for clients; less traffic on the exit link; and less load on the origin server.
text.zh: 好处有三个：缩短客户端的响应时间；减少出口的网络流量；减轻源服务器的负担。

title.en: How the hit rate affects average response time
title.zh: 命中率怎样影响平均响应时间

intro.en: The numbers are our own, set to see the trend, not measurements. The campus proxy is very close to you and a hit takes only 10 ms. On a miss, the proxy must also make a trip to the origin server, and that round trip is 190 ms, so 200 ms in all.
intro.zh: 数是我们自己设的，用来看趋势，不是测量值。校园里的代理离你很近，命中时只要 10 ms。未命中时，代理还要去一趟源服务器，那一趟往返 190 ms，所以总共 200 ms。

why.en: Hit: only back and forth between you and the proxy. Miss: add the trip from the proxy to the origin server.
why.zh: 命中：只在你和代理之间来回。未命中：多出代理到源服务器那一趟。

why.en: h is the hit rate, the fraction of requests that hit. The average time weights the two cases by their fractions.
why.zh: h 是命中率，即命中的请求占的比例。平均时间是两种情况按比例加权。

why.en: With six in ten hitting, the average drops from 200 ms to 86 ms.
why.zh: 六成命中，平均从 200 ms 降到 86 ms。

why.en: With nine in ten hitting, the average comes close to 10 ms.
why.zh: 九成命中，平均几乎贴近 10 ms。

why.en: Only requests that miss leave the campus to look for the origin server. At a hit rate of 0.6, exit traffic is down to 40%, and the origin server handles only that 40%.
why.zh: 没命中的请求才会走出学校去找源服务器。命中率 0.6 时，出口流量只剩 40%，源服务器也只需要处理这 40%。

outro.en: The higher the hit rate, the closer the average response time gets to the hit time, and the exit traffic and the pressure on the origin server fall together. The price: the copies in the cache may be out of date. The next page covers what to do.
outro.zh: 命中率越高，平均响应时间越接近命中时的时间，出口流量和源服务器的压力也一起降下来。代价是：缓存里的副本可能过时。下一页说怎么办。

title.en: What if a copy is out of date

text.en: A cache has just one constraint, but it is a serious one: it must stay fresh and consistent. If the object on the origin server changes while the cache still holds the old one, what then?
text.zh: 缓存的限制只有一条，却很要命：要保持新鲜和一致。源服务器上的对象改了，缓存里还是旧的，怎么办？

text.en: The way is the conditional GET. When the proxy holds a copy, it neither uses it directly nor refetches the whole thing, but asks one question: “My copy was modified at such-and-such a time. Has it been modified on your side since?”
text.zh: 办法是条件请求 (conditional GET)。代理手里有副本时，不直接用，也不整个重取，而是问一句：「我这份是某某时间改的，你那边之后改过吗？」

blocks.code:
GET /pic.gif HTTP/1.1
Host: www.someschool.edu
If-Modified-Since: Tue, 30 Oct 2007 17:00:02 GMT

HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified

caption.en: The time asked about is the Last-Modified from the response. If-Modified-Since doesn't appear in the slides; it is added here to make things clear.
caption.zh: 问的那个时间，就是响应里的 Last-Modified。If-Modified-Since 课件里没有出现，这里为了说清楚加上。

items.en: **Not modified**: the server replies 304 Not Modified, with no data. The proxy keeps using its copy, saving the transfer.
items.zh: **没改**：服务器回 304 Not Modified，不带数据。代理继续用手里的副本，省下了传输。

items.en: **Modified**: the server replies 200 OK with the new object. The proxy replaces the old copy.
items.zh: **改了**：服务器回 200 OK，带上新对象。代理换掉旧副本。

text.en: This is where 304 “the cached page is still valid” comes from, and it is also the use of Last-Modified in the response: it marks the object's “version”. A conditional request still costs 1 RTT to ask, and what it saves is file transfer time, especially worthwhile for large files.
text.zh: 这就是 304「缓存的页面仍然有效」的来历，也是响应里 Last-Modified 的用处：它是对象「版本」的记号。条件请求仍然要花 1 个 RTT 问一句，省下的是文件传输时间，对大文件特别划算。

title.en: Beyond the slides

body.en: The browser also has a cache of its own, checked before sending a request to the network. A proxy cache and a browser cache work in the same way.
body.zh: 浏览器自己也有一份缓存，在向网络发请求之前先查。代理缓存和浏览器缓存的做法是一样的。

title.en: Work out an average response time

prompt.en: Campus proxy: a hit responds in 10 ms, a miss in 200 ms. The measured hit rate is now 80%. What is the average response time in milliseconds?
prompt.zh: 校园代理：命中时响应 10 ms，未命中时 200 ms。现在统计到命中率是 80%。平均响应时间是多少毫秒？

hints.en: Average = hit rate × hit time + (1 - hit rate) × miss time.
hints.zh: 平均 = 命中率 × 命中的时间 + (1 - 命中率) × 未命中的时间。

explain.en: 0.8 × 10 + 0.2 × 200 = 8 + 40 = 48 ms. Compared with 200 ms without a cache, that is over four times faster; and only 20% of requests have to leave the campus to look for the origin server.
explain.zh: 0.8 × 10 + 0.2 × 200 = 8 + 40 = 48 ms。和没有缓存时的 200 ms 比，快了四倍多；而且只有 20% 的请求要走出学校去找源服务器。

title.en: Back to that click in the dorm

text.en: Walk through this lesson along that click on www.unimelb.edu.au:
text.zh: 把这一课沿着 www.unimelb.edu.au 那次点击走一遍：

items.en: DNS turns www.unimelb.edu.au into an IP (last lesson).
items.zh: DNS 把 www.unimelb.edu.au 变成 IP（上一课）。

items.en: The browser sets up a TCP connection to port 80 of that IP, costing 1 RTT.
items.zh: 浏览器和这个 IP 的 80 端口建一条 TCP 连接，花 1 个 RTT。

items.en: It sends a GET request: a request line plus header lines (Host says which website is wanted, and if you have visited before, a Cookie is attached too), and receives 200 OK and the HTML.
items.zh: 发 GET 请求：请求行加首部行（Host 说明要哪个网站，之前访问过的话还会带上 Cookie），收到 200 OK 和 HTML。

items.en: It reads the HTML, finds a batch of referenced objects, and keeps fetching them over the persistent connection, perhaps opening several connections at once too.
items.zh: 读 HTML，发现一批被引用的对象，在持久连接上继续取，可能还同时开几条连接。

items.en: Along the way it may meet a 301 move or a 304 cache-still-valid; a proxy's cache may also deliver the object directly.
items.zh: 路上也许遇到 301 搬家、304 缓存仍有效；代理的缓存也许直接把对象送了过来。

rows.en: A page is many objects; URL = host name + path
rows.zh: 一个页面是很多对象；URL = 主机名 + 路径

rows.en: One connection per object, 2 RTTs for each object
rows.zh: 一条连接一个对象，每个对象 2 个 RTT
持久 HTTP 与流水线

rows.en: Shake hands once; pipelining then sends requests together
rows.zh: 握一次手；流水线再把请求一起发出

rows.en: Request line, header lines, blank line, entity body; GET asks, POST hands over
rows.zh: 请求行、首部行、空行、实体体；GET 要，POST 交

rows.en: Status line, header lines, blank line, data; the first digit sets the class
rows.zh: 状态行、首部行、空行、数据；第一位定类

rows.en: A number; the real state is in the server's database
rows.zh: 一个编号，真正的状态在服务器的数据库里

rows.en: On a hit, return from nearby; on a miss, fetch for you; conditional requests keep things fresh
rows.zh: 命中就近返回，没命中替你去要；靠条件请求保持新鲜

text.en: One thing remains unsolved: all the HTTP messages along this road are plain text, and anyone on the way can read them. What to do about that is a matter for the last few lessons (HTTPS). The next lesson first looks at email and streaming media.
text.zh: 还有一件事没解决：这一路上所有的 HTTP 报文都是明文，谁在路上都能读。怎么办，是最后几课（HTTPS）的事。下一课先看电子邮件和流媒体。
